question: A bag holds 6 green marbles and 14 yellow marbles. Tom puts 5 more green marbles into the bag. What percentage of the marbles in the bag are green now?
hint: How many marbles are in the bag now, and how many of them are green?
solution: Now there are 6 + 5 = 11 green marbles among 20 + 5 = 25 marbles. 11 out of 25 is the same as 44 out of 100, so 44% are green.

A.text: 55% compares the 11 green marbles with the 20 marbles there were before, not with the 25 in the bag now.

B.text: 30% leaves out the 5 marbles Tom added: it is the green share before, 6 out of 20.

C.text: 56% is the share of yellow marbles now.

E.text: 5 is the number of marbles Tom added, not a percentage.

question: At a party, 60% of the guests chose vanilla ice cream and 30% chose chocolate. The other 3 guests chose strawberry. How many guests were at the party?
hint: What percentage of the guests chose strawberry?
solution: Vanilla and chocolate make 60% + 30% = 90%, so the 3 strawberry guests are the other 10%. If 10% is 3 guests, then 100% is 30 guests.

A.text: 18 is the guests who chose vanilla, only part of the party.

C.text: 27 is the guests who chose vanilla or chocolate; the 3 strawberry guests were at the party too.

D.text: 3 is the number of strawberry guests, copied from the question.

E.text: 10 is the strawberry share in per cent, not a number of guests; 10% is 3 guests.

question: A board game costs 200 coins. Its price goes up by 10%. A week later, the new price goes down by 10%. What does the game cost now?
hint: The second 10% is taken of which price?
solution: 10% of 200 is 20, so the price goes up to 220. 10% of 220 is 22, so it goes down to 220 - 22 = 198 coins.

A.text: 200 takes the fall as 10% of the old price, 20 coins, but it is 10% of 220, which is 22 coins.

B.text: 220 is the price after it went up; the fall a week later still has to come.

C.text: 242 raises the price a second time, but the second change was a fall.

D.text: 180 takes 10% off the old price and forgets that the price first went up.

question: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs 60 coins. What was its price before the discount?
hint: What percentage of the old price does the jacket cost now?
solution: After the discount the jacket costs 80% of its old price. 80% is four lots of 20%, so 20% is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 coins, and the old price is 5 × 15 = 75 coins.

B.text: 72 adds 20% of the new price, 12 coins, but the discount was 20% of the old price.

C.text: 80 adds 20 coins for the 20%, instead of splitting 60 into four parts of 20% each.

D.text: 48 takes a second 20% off, but the question goes back to the price before the discount.

E.text: 15 coins is the size of the discount, not the old price.

question: On a farm, 60% of the birds are hens, and 25% of the hens are brown. What percentage of all the birds on the farm are brown hens?
hint: Imagine the farm has 100 birds. How many of them are hens?
solution: Take 100 birds: 60 of them are hens. A quarter of 60 is 15, so 15 of the 100 birds are brown hens, which is 15%.

A.text: 25% is the brown share of the hens, not of all the birds.

B.text: 60% is all the hens, and only some of them are brown.

D.text: 85% adds 60% and 25%, but the 25% is a part of the 60%, not extra birds.

E.text: 35% takes 25% away from 60%, but the brown hens are a quarter of the hens, not what is left of them.

question: Lena has 15 more stickers than Max, and that is 25% more than Max has. By what percentage does Max have fewer stickers than Lena?
hint: How many stickers does Max have, and how many does Lena have?
solution: 15 stickers are 25% of Max's stickers, so Max has 4 × 15 = 60 and Lena has 75. Max has 15 fewer, and 15 out of 75 is 20%.

A.text: 25% compares the 15 stickers with Max's 60, but here they have to be compared with Lena's 75.

B.text: 15 is the number of extra stickers, not a percentage.

C.text: 80% is how much Max has compared with Lena, not how much less.

E.text: 125% compares Lena's stickers with Max's, the other way round.

question: In a basket, 25% of the apples are red. After 6 red apples are eaten, 10% of the apples left are red. How many apples were in the basket at first?
hint: The apples that are not red stay in the basket. What share of it are they before and after?
solution: The apples that are not red stay. At first there are 3 of them for every red apple, and later 9 for every red apple. So the red apples go from a third of the others to a ninth of them, and the 6 eaten apples are 2/9 of the others. That makes 27 other apples and 9 red ones: 36 apples at first.

A.text: 40 takes the drop from 25% to 10% as 15% of the first basket, but the 10% is of a smaller basket.

C.text: 9 is the red apples at first, only part of the basket.

D.text: 27 is the apples that are not red; the red ones were in the basket too.

E.text: 24 takes the 6 eaten apples as all of the red 25%, but 3 red apples are still left.

question: 20% of Mia's stamps is the same number of stamps as 30% of Sam's. Together they have 200 stamps. How many stamps does Mia have?
hint: Who has more stamps, Mia or Sam? Try a few ways of splitting 200.
solution: 20% is 2 tenths and 30% is 3 tenths, so 2 tenths of Mia's stamps equal 3 tenths of Sam's. That means Mia has 3 stamps for every 2 of Sam's, and 200 splits as 120 and 80. Check: 20% of 120 is 24, and 30% of 80 is 24.

A.text: 40 is 20% of all 200 stamps, not the number of Mia's stamps.

B.text: 80 is how many stamps Sam has.

C.text: 100 splits the stamps equally, but then 20% and 30% of them would not be the same number.

D.text: 24 is the equal number, 20% of Mia's stamps; her whole collection is five times that.

question: A bus carries fewer than 40 passengers, and exactly 35% of the passengers are children. How many adults are on the bus?
hint: For which numbers of passengers is 35% of them a whole number?
solution: 35% is 7 twentieths, so the number of passengers must divide by 20. Fewer than 40 leaves only 20 passengers: 7 children and 13 adults.

B.text: 20 is all the passengers, children as well as adults.

C.text: 7 is the number of children on the bus.

D.text: 26 comes from a bus of 40 passengers, but the bus carries fewer than 40.

E.text: 35 is the children's percentage, not a number of people.
